description: The image displays two stacked line plots illustrating the behavior of two variables — *n* (top plot) and *Size_run* (bottom plot) — as functions of a variable *m*, with a marked reference point *m₀* on the x-axis. Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled *m*, ranging from 0 to beyond *m₀*, with tick marks at regular intervals; the scale appears linear. The top plot’s y-axis is labeled *n*, with labeled horizontal dashed lines at *w*, *c − a − s*, and *c − a*, indicating key thresholds. The plotted line begins at the origin (0,0), rises linearly to *c − a*, then drops vertically to *w*, and repeats this sawtooth pattern with decreasing amplitude after *m₀*, eventually stabilizing near *w*. The bottom plot’s y-axis is labeled *Size_run*, with dashed lines at *w + a + s* and *c*. The line here also starts at (0,0), rises linearly to *c*, drops vertically to *w + a + s*, and repeats the sawtooth pattern, similarly dampening after *m₀* and approaching *w + a + s*. Both plots use solid black lines with sharp vertical drops and diagonal ascents, visually representing periodic resets or compression events in the context of segment-based LLM acceleration as described in the paper “SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.”
